title: Unify button interaction choreography and chart palette deltas for density-aware system
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
- Over time our component library has accumulated separate token sets for interactive controls and chart palettes. This has introduced small but frequent inconsistencies between button states and chart datum contrast when apps switch between compact (dense) and relaxed (airy) density modes.

Goal:
- Consolidate interaction "ink" and elevation tokens so button, pill, and icon controls share a predictable choreography across density scopes.
- Introduce a Delta Palette system for charts: a base semantic ramp plus small density-aware deltas to ensure datapoints maintain contrast and perceived prominence relative to UI chrome.

Scope (what's in):
- Token additions: interaction-ink.[default|hover|press|focus], micro-shadow.[compact|default|airy], surface-contrast.delta.[compact|airy] for charts.
- Mapping: wire button states (primary/secondary/tertiary) to the interaction-ink tokens and micro-shadow tokens.
- Chart palettes: create delta variants (chart-accent.delta-1, -2) that offset base accents by luminance and saturation to keep accessible contrast against changing surface tones.
- Docs & migration guide for frontend engineers (codemod + examples).

What's out of scope for this ticket:
- Full token rename across entire product (we'll do phased migrations).
- Reworking iconography or motion primitives beyond hover/press opacity and shadow.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New tokens exist in the token registry and are documented with visual examples for compact and airy modes.
2) Buttons (all variants) use the new interaction-ink tokens for default/hover/press/focus. Visual regressions limited to intended deltas only.
3) Chart palettes expose delta variants and examples for common chart types (line, bar, scatter) demonstrating preserved contrast at small point sizes.
4) Automated codemod provided to replace old ink/shadow tokens with new tokens for primary button and charts (example PR in GH).
5) Accessibility: all button states meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast when measured against surface tokens in both density modes. Chart datapoints meet 3:1 contrast for contextual markings and 4.5:1 for emphasis markings.

Design proposal (summary):
- Interaction ink tokens are semantic (ink.primary, ink.secondary, ink.ghost) with state variants: ink.*.rest, ink.*.hover, ink.*.active, ink.*.focus-ring. These map to color + alpha overlays (not full replacements) to preserve base surface texture.
- Micro-shadow tokens are shallow (0–2px) in compact, moderate (2–6px) in default, and soft (6–12px) in airy. Purpose-built to avoid visual jumps when density toggles.
- Chart delta palettes are computed: baseAccent + deltaLuminance (-6% compact, +6% airy) + deltaSaturation (±4%). We provide 6 delta levels for multi-series charts.

Engineering notes / runtime considerations:
- Prefer alpha overlays for ink tokens to preserve anti-aliasing on text and icons and to play well with GPU compositing.
- Chart palette deltas will be provided as CSS variables and JSON model palettes; runtime selection occurs in the chart renderer based on the density token.
- Codemod will target common tokens: legacy-ink-*/legacy-shadow-* -> new token equivalents. Edge cases flagged for manual review will be output as a migration report.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Option A: rename all tokens centrally now (bigger sweep, faster consistency) vs Option B: introduce new tokens and opt-in mapping (safer, incremental). We chose Option B to reduce cross-repo churn and allow staggered QA.
- Using alpha overlay vs hard color swap: overlays reduce abrupt typographic color shifts but can have subtle differences on patterned backgrounds; measured visually and accepted for the sake of preserving texture.

Testing plan:
- Visual QA: Percy snapshot tests for a button matrix across densities and chart fixtures (line/bar/scatter) across light/dark and compact/airy.
- Contrast audits: automated color contrast checks against token matrix.
- Canary rollout: expose new tokens behind feature flag; request opt-in from 3 internal apps/teams.

Migration steps (high level):
1) Land token definitions and docs in tokens repo (this ticket).
2) Frontend: update button component to consume new tokens behind a flag.
3) Charts: introduce delta variants in chart config and add mapping in chart renderer.
4) Run codemod on web monorepo targeting common usages; open PRs per package for review.
5) Release design-tokens-2025Q2 with migration instructions and rollback plan.

Open questions / blockers:
- Do platform teams prefer deltas exposed as absolute hex values or as relative transforms (luminance/saturation) that the chart library applies at runtime? (Engineering preference currently leans runtime transforms for flexibility.)
- Do we include motion-reduced variants of micro-shadow or document that motion-safe should only affect motion tokens? (Motion team requested explicit motion-reduced shadow tokens; we may add this in follow-up.)

Links & artifacts:
- Design spec (FigJam): https://redwood.invisionapp.com/f/design-tokens/ink-and-delta-palettes
- Token registry PR: https://github.com/redwood/tokens/pull/542 (WIP)
- Codemod prototype: https://github.com/redwood/tooling/tree/main/codemods/ink-migration (prototype script + README)
- Example chart PR: https://github.com/redwood/charts/pull/198 (draft)

Progress updates:
- 2025-02-10 (Ava Martinez): Ticket created with initial proposal; sketched delta rules and button matrix.
- 2025-02-14 (Liam Chen): Reviewed with frontend leads. Agreed on incremental rollout and runtime transform approach for chart deltas.
- 2025-02-20 (Ava Martinez): Completed first pass tokens in tokens repo; PR opened (link above). Added visual examples for compact/default/airy.
- 2025-02-26 (Liam Chen): Prototype codemod created and run against internal demo app; produced migration report with ~18 manual flags.
- 2025-03-02 (Liam Chen): Implemented button component behind feature flag and added Percy snapshots. Found a contrast edge for tertiary button on low-contrast surfaces; created follow-up sub-issue DES-46305.

Follow-ups / sub-issues:
- DES-46305: resolve tertiary button contrast with muted surfaces in compact mode (created).
- DES-46410: introduce explicit motion-reduced micro-shadow tokens (backlog).

Acceptance checklist (to land):
- [ ] Token PR merged
- [ ] Button component PR merged and feature-flagged
- [ ] Chart delta PR merged with runtime transforms
- [ ] Codemod published and sample migration PRs opened
- [ ] Percy/regression suite green for flagged apps

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the visual relationship between shadow intensity and ink overlays in compact mode; small changes amplify at small sizes.
- The delta values are deliberately conservative; if you need more separation for specific charts, add emphasis tokens rather than widen global deltas.

Estimated roll timeline:
- Token landing: 1 week after approvals
- Component updates + codemod: 2–3 weeks
- Canary testing: 2 weeks
- Full rollout: dependent on app opt-ins, target end of Q2 2025
